Position description The Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of California, Davis invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in hard condensed matter experimental physics. We seek candidates with an outstanding research record and the potential to establish a highly visible, externally funded program. Candidates from all areas of experimental condensed matter physics are encouraged to apply. Areas of interest include quantum materials and emergent phenomena; strongly correlated and topological systems; superconductivity and magnetism; low-dimensional, nanoscale, and mesoscopic systems; nonequilibrium and ultrafast phenomena; quantum transport and devices; and novel experimental techniques, instrumentation, or materials platforms. We especially welcome research that complements or expands existing strengths and fosters collaboration across UC Davis. The successful candidate will develop an independent, internationally recognized research program; teach effectively at the undergraduate and graduate levels; mentor students; contribute to the condensed matter community; and participate in departmental, university, and professional service. Candidates must have a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in physics or a closely related field by the time of application. UC Davis offers a collaborative environment with strengths in quantum materials, materials synthesis, spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, low-temperature physics, optical and transport measurements, nanostructures, and quantum phenomena, together with a strong condensed matter theory community and interdisciplinary connections across Materials Science and Engineering, Chemistry, Electrical and Computer Engineering, and other departments. Faculty have access to extensive shared infrastructure, including the Center for Nano-MicroManufacturing (CNM2), the Advanced Materials Characterization and Testing Laboratory (AMCaT), and a departmental helium recovery and liquefaction facility, as well as major national user facilities including the Advanced Light Source and Molecular Foundry at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and SSRL and LCLS at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory. The successful candidate will join a mature experimental and theoretical condensed matter community while helping shape its next phase through new scientific directions, techniques, and capabilities. Job Posting Title: Assistant Professor - Human Geography Position Type: Faculty Department: LSUAM HSS - School of Geography and Anthropology (Jill C Trepanier (00002085)) Work Location: W0227 Howe Russell Kniffen West Geoscience Complex Pay Grade: Academic Job Description: The Department of Geography and Anthropology at Louisiana State University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Human Geography specializing in Geographic Information Science and Technology (GISc&T) and geospatial data science. We seek a scholar with strong expertise in GISc&T and advanced geospatial methods to answer complex societal and human-environment questions. Relevant methodological expertise may include spatial-temporal analysis, geospatial data science, remote sensing, GeoAI, WebGIS, geovisualization, or related computational approaches. Candidates are not expected to specialize in all these areas. We are particularly interested in candidates who can expand the department's methodological capacity and contribute to innovative applications of geospatial technologies in research and teaching. The substantive area of specialization is open, but the successful candidate's scholarship must have a strong human-geographic dimension . Research areas may include, but are not limited to, health and well-being, population and inequality, food systems, energy and infrastructure, environmental change, hazards and disaster vulnerability, community resilience, critical GIS, or other societally relevant dimensions of human-environment interaction. We welcome scholarship that uses geospatial methods not simply as technical tools, but to advance understanding of important social, spatial, and environmental problems. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate instruction in GISc&T, spatial-temporal analysis, and environmental studies , while developing courses in their areas of methodological and topical expertise. The position will also offer opportunities to contribute to and collaborate with the department's Environmental Studies and Disaster Science and Management areas and to strengthen interdisciplinary geospatial training across departmental programs in both geography and anthropology. The successful candidate will be expected to develop an externally fundable research program; teach undergraduate and graduate courses; mentor undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students; and contribute to the department's growing emphasis on interdisciplinary and community-engaged scholarship. Opportunities exist for collaboration across geography and anthropology and with programs and units throughout LSU, such as the South Central Climate Adaptation Science Center. A PhD in human geography, geographic information science, or a closely related field with a strong human-geographic dimension is required or must be completed by the start of the appointment. We seek candidates with strong expertise in one or more areas of computational and algorithmic methods; scientific artificial intelligence and machine learning; multiscale modeling and simulation; large-scale optimization; and hybrid, physics, and/or data-driven approaches for the design, operation, control, and decision-making under uncertainty in processing systems. Research applications may include sustainable chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and fuels, resilient energy systems, advanced manufacturing, the circular economy, and other emerging challenges in chemical and process systems engineering. The successful candidate is expected to establish and maintain a nationally recognized, externally funded research program at the intersection of process systems engineering, chemical engineering, and decision science. Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to, multiscale modeling; optimization; and computational methods for the design, operation, control, and decision-making under uncertainty in processing systems. The successful candidate will be expected to conduct original, scholary research; build self-sustaining research programs; teach both graduate and undergraduate courses and mentor students; and contribute an appropriate degree of service to the Department, College, University, and profession. Candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring at both undergraduate and graduate levels, as well as active engagement in departmental, college, and professional service. The position offers extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across Texas A&M’s strengths in engineering, life sciences, and agriculture, and aligns with university-wide investments in biomanufacturing and sustainability. Qualifications Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Process Systems Engineering, or a closely related field, with an outstanding record of scholarly achievement, ability to secure competitive research funding, and evidence of effective teaching and mentorship. Application Instructions Applicants must submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a personal Statement (your statement should include your philosophy and plans for research, teaching, and service as applicable), and a list of four contact references (including postal addresses, phone numbers and email addresses) by applying for this specific position at https://apply.interfolio.com/192370. job_60d29d943422da88: Description The goal of the BC Postdoctoral Research Grants program is to fund research and educational opportunities so that postdocs at BC have an opportunity to gain skills and experience important for their overall goals in their postdoctoral training. Travel funding for conferences is specifically excluded from this program. There are two areas of funding: Research: Funding may be used to support the postdoc’s own research, meaning it cannot be put toward their PI’s lab’s general project budget. It also cannot be used toward salary. The postdoc may use the funding to purchase software or equipment specific to their independent work, to compensate research participants, to pay a stipend to a graduate or undergraduate research assistant, or to support an entire study on which the postdoc is the lead researcher. It may also be used to collect pilot data that the postdoc plans to use in a future grant application. A budget of no more than $2,500 can be requested for research. Training: While these grants cannot be used for conference travel, they can be used toward travel for (1) training opportunities (such as a workshop to learn a methodology or instrument) or (2) to visit another lab at a different institution. A budget of no more than $1,500 can be requested for travel.

JOB DESCRIPTION:
University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB Health) – Galveston, Texas
UTMB Health is a $2.2 billion health science center comprised of five hospitals, an extensive network of outpatient clinics, and Schools of Medicine, Nursing, Health Professions, Public and Population Health, as well as a Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, three institutes and over 10 exceptional research centers. UTMB has a long and remarkable history of advancing health sciences education, research, and patient care. It was the first academic health center in Texas and is home to the state’s first schools of medicine, nursing, and allied health sciences. UTMB is also home to the Galveston National Laboratory, one of only two laboratories conducting research on a university campus at the BSL-4 level in the U.S. Overall research funding has increased 20% over the past five years to $132 million and UTMB ranks 54th nationally in NIH funding among medical schools. UTMB also ranks as a five-star hospital by Vizient, for superior performance in providing high quality care.
The UTMB Department of Family Medicine was founded as an independent department in 1971 but existed prior to that as a division of the Department of Preventive Medicine and Population Health. Family Medicine faculty provide medical care to Galveston County residents through its three clinics, located on the UTMB Galveston campus, on the western end of Galveston Island, and in Dickinson, Texas, and through its inpatient service at the new Jennie Sealy Hospital in Galveston, Texas. Additional services are rendered at the Gulf Health Care Center nursing home and the Galveston County Health District's Coastal Health & Wellness. At present the Department includes programs in medical student education, residency, faculty development, and research.
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
This position will be 90% clinical and 10% education and will see patients in the clinic primarily at our Galveston Island locations. He/she will provide direct patient care and will provide teaching and supervision of Family Medicine residents. This physician may share on-call responsibilities, including evening and weekend hours, precept medical students and cover other clinical services as needed. He/she may provide comprehensive health care with enhanced access for patients within a patient-centered medical home clinical model. This faculty will have 90% clinical effort and practice primarily at the Island West Clinic (IW) but will also rotate through the Island West (IE) or Dickinson Family Medicine Clinics as departmental need arises.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
• MD or DO degree
• A strong commitment to research, patient care, medical student, and resident education.
• U.S. Citizenship or Employment Authorization to work in the U.S.
SALARY:
Commensurate with experience.
What UTMB has to offer potential candidates:
• A high quality academic and clinical program.
• Participation in medical student, resident, and fellow education and training.
• Leadership and career advancement opportunities.
• Research participation is highly encouraged and supported.
• Competitive salary with a generous bonus and benefits package.
Income Package : Salary is commensurate with Academic rank, experience, and qualifications. In addition, UTMB offers a superior benefits package, an excellent retirement program, a relocation allowance as well as other potential incentives.
Living in communities served by UTMB Health: UTMB’s main campus is located on Galveston Island which is known for its 32 miles of beaches all along the Texas Gulf Coast. Enjoy the island life with moderate temperatures, year-round activities, affordable cost of living and only 50 minutes from all the amenities that Houston has to offer! Enjoy our family culture and collaborative environment while you work, live, & play on sunny Galveston Island! Securing water has become a defining challenge of the century, and Michigan is where that challenge is most sharply concentrated. The state holds the world's largest freshwater system, anchors a diverse agricultural economy dependent on water, and is now attracting a wave of water-intensive industry — data centers, EV battery production, and advanced manufacturing — that is creating unprecedented and unevenly distributed demand. Floods, droughts, and weather extremes across the Great Lakes region are growing more frequent and severe, straining aging infrastructure and agricultural systems. MSU is uniquely positioned at this precise intersection of freshwater abundance, agricultural mission, and industrial water demand — and meeting these challenges is fundamentally an engineering problem. We welcome candidates whose research and teaching address these critical societal challenges, particularly in areas such as flood and drought forecasting, controllable urban water systems, resilient infrastructure, and data-driven management of rivers, lakes, and groundwater. This includes the coupling of process-based hydrologic and hydrodynamic modeling with AI, machine learning, remote sensing, high-performance computing, and real-time data infrastructure. Distinct opportunities also exist in physics-informed AI, digital twins of watersheds and water infrastructure, and smart-sensored water systems grounded in a real freshwater-agriculture-industry setting. We welcome applications at the rank of Assistant Professor, though outstanding candidates at Associate or Full Professor level are also encouraged to apply. This will be a full-time, academic-year appointment in the tenure system, with tenure, if appropriate, at a salary commensurate with the candidate’s background and experience. The Instructor of Nursing and Simulation Coordinator is responsible for the upkeep of simulation equipment, supplies, standardized patients, simulation technologies, skills laboratories, simulation-based clinical replacement experiences, faculty support related to simulation, and compliance with INACSL Standards of Best Practice, CCNE standards, and Oregon State Board of Nursing regulations. Primary Job Duties: Teach assigned nursing courses (6 credits per year) within the Prelicensure BSN curriculum. Coordinate simulation and skills laboratory activities across all levels of the Prelicensure BSN curriculum. Collaborate with faculty and administration to design, implement, revise, and evaluate simulation scenarios aligned with course outcomes, AACN (2026) Essentials, and QSEN competencies; maintain compliance with INACSL Healthcare Simulation Standards of Best Practice; and support CCNE accreditation and Oregon State Board of Nursing (OSBN) regulatory compliance activities. In collaboration with nursing faculty assist with simulation pre-briefing, simulation experiences, and debriefing using evidence-based methodologies. In collaboration with nursing faculty, assist with the development of realistic simulation experiences that promote clinical judgment, critical thinking, communication, teamwork, and patient safety. Prepare simulation and skills laboratories, equipment, supplies, and standardized patients to support laboratory and simulation learning activities. Maintain organization of the simulation and skills laboratories, ensuring equipment, supplies, and teaching materials are properly stored, inventoried, and readily accessible. Monitor simulation supply inventories and coordinate purchasing recommendations. Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and coordinate repair of high-fidelity simulators, audiovisual systems, task trainers, and simulation technology. Assist when needed with development and implementation of simulation policies, procedures, and quality improvement initiatives. Maintain simulation laboratory schedules and coordinate simulation space utilization in accordance with the Dean of Nursing. Support nursing faculty in simulation technology, simulation facilitation, and debriefing best practices. Support student remediation, competency validation, and skills laboratory activities. Collect and maintain simulation utilization data, student participation records, and assessment information. Support orientation activities, open laboratory sessions, student skills workshops, and university-wide events. Following each laboratory, simulation, and skills session, restores and maintains the simulation and skills laboratories in a clean, organized, and patient-ready condition. Participate in professional organizations and maintain current knowledge of simulation standards and best practices. Exhibit excellent communication skills in all interactions with administrators, faculty, staff, and students.
